blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_146
blocks.text: Weather conditions and acquisition of seismic data

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_147
blocks.text: Weather conditions affect the acquisition of seismic data. Normally, one is dependent on good weather and wave heights of less than 2 to 4 metres to ensure a satisfactory quality of the data. If weather conditions are poor, the seismic vessel has to wait for better weather. Wave height in particular is an important factor in seismic acquisitions, which means that acquisition is halted if the wave height is too high. The vulnerability of seismic data acquisition to wave height depends on the water depth of the streamers. While acquisition with streamers deeper in the water column is less dependent on wave height, deep streamers normally also weaken the quality of the seismic data.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_148
blocks.text: Average weather conditions vary throughout the year, which means that acquisition of seismic data is seasonal. In the summer months, lower average wave height and better weather can normally be expected, ensuring high acquisition uptime and cost-effective acquisition. seismic companies often send their ships overseas during the winter, due to limited opportunity for seismic acquisitions during the season.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_149
blocks.text: Fishery activities

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_150
blocks.text: Fisheries can be divided into many different types, based on area and time of year, type and size of vessel and, not least, the stocks that are fished.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_151
blocks.text: The cases where conflicts have occurred between seismic vessels and fishing vessels largely pertain to seasonal fisheries. Typical seasonal fisheries involve harvesting fish concentrated in particular areas at particular times, either on spawning grounds, en route to spawning grounds or in concentrated feeding areas. Fishing for cod that feed on capelin en route to spawning grounds off the coast of Finnmark is one example, while the spring cod fishery in Lofoten is an example of fishing for cod migrating to spawn and on spawning grounds. Seasonal fisheries use a variety of different gear and types of vessels, from the smallest boats with a single fisherman on board to large ocean-going combined seiner/trawlers.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_152
blocks.text: Norwegian fishing and hunting take place in the Norwegian economic zone, in other countries' zones and in international waters. Based on scientific data from the Institute of Marine Research and other national marine research institutes, the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES) undertakes stock assessments and provides advice on quotas. The quota advice forms the basis for Norway's annual fisheries negotiations with other countries and the national quota allocation.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_153
blocks.text: Annual regulations relating to quota size, allocation between vessel groups, technical aspects, etc. are laid down for each fishery and hunting activity. Proposals for regulations are drawn up by the Directorate of Fisheries and established by the Ministry of Fisheries and Coastal Affairs. The regulations for most fisheries are laid down at the beginning of the year.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_154
blocks.text: Norway also hunts some minke whales under catch quotas set by the Ministry of Fisheries and Coastal Affairs based on advice from the International Whaling Commission (IWC). Hunting takes place from April to August.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_155
blocks.text: By 31 December 2012, Norway had 6.214 fishing vessels registered in the Register of Fishing Vessels. The total fishing and hunting volume in 2012 was just over 2.1 million tonnes.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_156
blocks.text: Most fisheries are seasonal. Although the regulations for some species permit fishing year round, fishing is generally limited to one or more periods of the year. This is mainly due to the fact that it is only then and there that a particular species can be profitably harvested. Fishing can essentially be divided into two groups: passive gear fishing and active gear fishing.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_157
blocks.text: Passive or fixed gear is gear where one or both ends are anchored at the sea bottom and marked with surface buoys displaying the fishing vessel's registration number. Nets and lines are the most important fishing gear in this group. Fishing with such gear takes place both close to the coast with smaller vessels and larger vessels at sea. The extent of the gear can vary from chains of nets with a length of 0.5 km to a single row of lines of up to 75 km. Such gear is usually set and retrieved once a day.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_158
blocks.text: Active fishing gear is characterised as fishing gear that must seek out fish to catch it. In practice, this means that satisfactory stocks of fish must be registered before fishing gear is deployed. The duration of the catching operation for gear in this group varies between 1-6 hours. Trawls, purse seines and Danish seines are the most important gear in this category.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_159
blocks.text: The Directorate of Fisheries has prepared more detailed information on the various fisheries. This is available in Norwegian and English on NPD’s website under seismic: http://www.npd.no/en/Topics/seismic/Description-ofrelevant-fishing-gear/

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_160
blocks.text: How are fish and the fishing industry affected by seismic acquisition? How are fish stocks affected by seismic surveys?

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_161
blocks.text: The sound waves transmitted through the water during the acquisition of seismic data can affect marine organisms directly (physiologically) or indirectly (behavioural influence).

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_162
blocks.text: Direct effects - fish, eggs, larvae and fry

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_163
blocks.text: Fish exposed to sound waves from seismic acquisition will attempt to swim away from the source. Except for the metres closest to the sound source, adult fish are not directly injured by seismic sound waves.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_164
blocks.text: Eggs, larvae and fry do not have the same ability as large fish to escape the sound source. The sound energy from seismic activity can injure or kill larvae and fry near (less than five metres) the source by causing injuries to hearing and the kidneys, heart and swim bladder. 20 metres away there is very little likelihood that fry suffer damage. The natural mortality of larvae and fry is so high that the negative effect of seismic activity is small in comparison, and the consequences at the population level are considered insignificant and the uncertainty is negligible. On this basis, no restrictions are placed on seismic surveys out of consideration to injuries to fish eggs, larvae and fry.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_165
blocks.text: Indirect impact - spawning production

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_166
blocks.text: Fish react to sound in various ways. The weakest form of behavioural response is small changes in swimming activity where the fish changes direction and increases swimming speed, while the most powerful form of behaviour in response to sound is a quick flight reaction.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_167
blocks.text: The success of spawning could conceivably be affected if, during migration to spawning grounds or during spawning, the fish change behaviour due to acquisition of seismic data. The spawning migration pattern may change and spawning may be more or less displaced in time and space. Consequently, the larvae may miss the time window of optimal biological conditions for survival and growth.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_168
blocks.text: Restrictions on seismic activity have therefore been implemented in areas with important spawning grounds and in areas when concentrated spawning migrations take place. Time and area restrictions are block specific and are stipulated in the the individual licensing round announcements.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_169
blocks.text: How do seismic surveys affect fishing?

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_170
blocks.text: The acquisition of seismic data impacts fisheries both by area use in that seismic vessels use gear in the sea that requires a large amount of space and by seismic shooting, which could scare the fish away. Consequently, the acquisition of seismic data may in some situations lead to lost catches and catch income or increased fishing time and higher operating costs.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_171
blocks.text: However, some fisheries are more at risk than others; in particular, this applies to small vessels with short fishing seasons and a limited action radius.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_172
blocks.text: Startle effect

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_173
blocks.text: The issue of how the acquisition of seismic data impacts fish and the practice of fishing has been the subject of considerable attention for many years.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_174
blocks.text: An important question with respect to the startle effect on fish is how far away from the sound source the effect manifests itself. There is relatively little research on the startle effect. Research reports provide different results and are also somewhat contradictory, which has led to affected commercial parties having different views on the issue of minimum distance. However, how far and how the sound waves propagate depends on the prevailing horizontal and vertical salinity and temperature conditions. These change throughout the year and often from region to region. The authorities have therefore not determined a general minimum distance between seismic surveys and fishery activities, fish farming and hunting, but the regulations contain requirements that vessels carrying out seismic surveys must keep an appropriate distance to vessels engaged in fishing and from fixed and floating fishing gear, cf. Chapter 6.4.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_175
blocks.text: Relatively few studies have been carried out on the startle effect, and results vary from species to species. For example, the Institute of Marine Research conducted a survey on the Nordkapp bank in 1992, where reduced trawl catches were recorded 18 nautical miles from the seismic vessel. In the summer of 2009, the Institute of Marine Research conducted a so-called consequential research project in conjunction with NPD's acquisition of seismic data outside Lofoten and Vesterålen. The results here showed that fish behaviour and catches changed. Catches both increased and decreased depending on the method of fishing. There were no reports of any specific distance for the startle effect, but it was significantly less than the one observed on the Nordkapp bank. Experiments have also shown that seismic surveys per se do not damage marine life if the distance from the sound source is more than 5 metres.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_176
blocks.text: For example, mackerel is a shoal fish that swims relatively high up in the water where it can be caught with trolling lines. It is a fast-swimming fish that can easily move away from an area if it is startled.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_177
blocks.text: Area occupation

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_178
blocks.text: Potential challenges related to the area occupied by the acquisition of seismic data are most relevant for the part of the fishing fleet that has a limited action radius and during seasonal fisheries.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_179
blocks.text: The Marine Resources Act and the Petroleum Act and Regulations provide guidelines for the obligation on seismic vessels to yield and other factors such as maintaining a safe distance to fixed fishing gear and fishing vessels in fisheries. Moreover, the general maritime rules apply, provided that they apply only to avoid collision between vessels.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_180
blocks.text: Unlike what is the case for fixed facilities, the Petroleum Regulations do not require a formal safety zone to be established around seismic vessels.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_181
blocks.text: Regulation of seismic activity

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_182
blocks.text: A number of measures have been implemented in recent years to reduce the potential for possible conflicts between fisheries and seismic surveys. For those cases where losses still occur in the performance of fishery activities, a claim for compensation may be submitted, cf. the discussion of the compensation scheme in Chapter 10.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_183
blocks.text: Requirement for authorisation

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_184
blocks.text: According to the Petroleum Act, none other than the State may conduct petroleum activities without authorisation. This means that anyone who acquires seismic data in connection with petroleum activities must be authorised pursuant to the Petroleum Act. Such permission may be either an exploration or a production licence2.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_185
blocks.text: A prerequisite for obtaining an exploration or production licence is that the area in question has been formally opened for petroleum activities.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_186
blocks.text: Exploration licence3

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_187
blocks.text: Exploration licences are awarded by the Norwegian Petroleum Directorate4. An exploration licence entitles the holder to explore for petroleum, i.e. geological, petrophysical, geophysical, geochemical and geotechnical activities, including shallow drilling, as well as the operation and use of facilities to the extent they are used for exploration. The licence is not exclusive. This means that several companies may be entitled to conduct surveys in the same area.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_188
blocks.text: An exploration licence may, in principle, include the entire Norwegian Continental Shelf, except for those areas that are not opened and areas awarded by production licences5. Licences may be granted for up to 3 years.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_189
blocks.text: Production licence6

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_190
blocks.text: Production licences are awarded by the King in Council. The production license gives the licensee an exclusive right to survey and carry out exploratory drilling and production of petroleum resources in the area covered by the licence. This means that only the licensee may conduct petroleum activities within the area covered by the licence. The production licence thus provides more extensive rights than an exploration licence.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_191
blocks.text: The duration of a production licence is determined in the individual licence. Section 1-3 of the Petroleum Act

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_192
blocks.text: seismic data may also be acquired in connection with route and seabed surveys, cf. Section 30 of the Petroleum Regulations, cf. Section 7 of the Resource Management Regulations, but such surveys are very limited in extent.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_193
blocks.text: Section 2-1 of the Petroleum Act

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_194
blocks.text: By law, the authority to grant exploration licences is vested in the Ministry, which has delegated the authority to the NPD.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_195
blocks.text: Section 2-2 of the Petroleum Act Section 3-3 of the Petroleum Act

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_196
blocks.text: Co-existence with other industries

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_197
blocks.text: Petroleum activities shall be conducted in a prudent manner, in co-existence with other industries. This important overall requirement for prudent activities is enshrined in Section 10-1 of the Act.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_198
blocks.text: Section 10-1, second paragraph, first sentence of the Petroleum Act reads:

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_199
blocks.text: The petroleum activities must not unnecessarily or to an unreasonable extent impede or obstruct shipping, fishing, aviation or other activities, or cause damage or threat of damage to pipelines, cables or other subsea facilities.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_200
blocks.text: This implies that the actors engaged in the petroleum industry must take other industries and users of the sea into account when they plan their activities.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_201
blocks.text: In relation to the fishing industry, this means that the licensee, before conducting a seismic survey, must decide whether the survey could have been undertaken in a different place, at another time or in a manner that would have been better for fishermen, without having significant practical or economic consequences for the licensee. If licensees have not included such considerations and assessments in their planning, it could be difficult to assess whether the survey unnecessarily complicates or impedes other business interests. It is therefore important that licensees demonstrate and document that they have taken these factors into account in their planning. The Institute of Marine Research and the Directorate of Fisheries can assist licensees with relevant information, and early contact with them is recommended.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_202
blocks.text: If a licensee does not comply with the provisions of Section 10-1 of the Petroleum Act, it could provide a basis for the Government to intervene and suspend activities7. The cause of an injunction to suspend activities may be violation of both the first and second subsections of Section 10-1. Such injunctions to suspend activities are invasive and will have major economic consequences. The Act therefore stipulates that any suspension of activities is subject to "special circumstances". The Norwegian Oil and Gas Association has published Recommended guidelines for Coexistence with the fishing sector when conducting seismic surveys, which offers considerable advice and suggestions on how to achieve coexistence. It is recommended that planning is started early, preferably the year before the planned start of a seismic acquisition, and no later than early that same year. The work going on in the early planning phase is important for achieving good coexistence, and it is recommended in this phase that the operator of the acquisition:

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_203
blocks.text: Establish an overview of all stakeholders, Establish a list of other acquisition activities planned in the same area at the same time, Establish an overview of fishery activities and any spawning and spawning migration in the area, Establish contact with relevant fisheries organisations,

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_204
blocks.text: Make its own organisation aware of the conditions surrounding the acquisition of seismic data in Norway.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_205
blocks.text: In addition, the guideline describes recommended and regulatory measures in later planning phases and during implementation of the acquisition.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_206
blocks.text: Cf. Section 10-1, third subsection of the Petroleum Act

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_207
blocks.text: The authorities see the guideline as a good and important tool, and require the petroleum industry to follow the guidelines faithfully.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_208
blocks.text: However, it cannot be expected that all seismic acquisitions only take place during periods of low fishing activity. Weather conditions and time constraints due, for instance, to spawning can imply that the licensee has a very limited amount of time to conduct the surveys, and thus must conduct the surveys even though there are substantial fishery activities in the area.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_209
blocks.text: Time and area restrictions

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_210
blocks.text: seismic has little effect on eggs, larvae and fry, but can affect fish behaviour and migration patterns, adversely affecting spawning production. Time limits have therefore been introduced for seismic activity in areas with important spawning grounds and in areas where there are concentrated spawning migrations.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_211
blocks.text: Time and area restrictions are in relation to the individual block and are stated in the wording of the individual licensing round announcements.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_212
blocks.text: Safe distance - Section 5, first subsection of the Resource Management Regulations: Section 5, first subsection of the Resource Management Regulations, reads:

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_213
blocks.text: "Vessels carrying out seismic surveys shall maintain a safe distance from vessels carrying out fishing activities and from fixed and floating fishing gear. Particular attention must be exercised when an accumulation of fishing vessels is observed."

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_214
blocks.text: This means that the seismic vessels shall keep such good distance to fishing vessels that no ongoing fisheries are unduly affected or that deployed fishing gear is physically destroyed.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_215
blocks.text: Marine Resources Act

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_216
blocks.text: The Act relating to the management of wild living marine resources (Marine Resources Act) aims to ensure sustainable and socio-economically profitable management of wild living marine resources and associated genetic material, and to contribute to securing employment and settlement in coastal communities.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_217
blocks.text: Section 24 of the Act deals with the rules of due care by the following: "Any person arriving at harvesting grounds where gear has been set shall acquaint himself with the location of such gear. All persons shall conduct themselves in such a way that fishing gear is not damaged or unnecessarily endangered. It is prohibited to impede harvesting or spoil harvesting opportunities by means of shooting, noise or other improper conduct. The Ministry may adopt further provisions on the manoeuvring of vessels and conduct on harvesting grounds."

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_218
blocks.text: The ban must be viewed in light of the materiality criterion, cf. also Chapter 6.4 and the compensation provisions in Chapter 10.2.1 and 10.2.2.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_219
blocks.text: Other matters that are regulated

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_220
blocks.text: Requirements for fishery experts on board the seismic vessel, reporting system, tracking seismic vessels and the compensation scheme for Norwegian fishermen are also regulated in the Petroleum Regulations. These are important and often comprehensive rules, and are therefore referred to as separate topics in the following chapters.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_221
blocks.text: Mackerel fishing and seismic acquisition the summer of 2012

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_222
blocks.text: In connection with mackerel fishing and seismic surveys on Tampen the summer of 2012, the Norwegian Fishermen's Association and Statoil agreed to carry out a pilot project.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_223
blocks.text: The pilot project involved close monitoring of the inflow and distribution of mackerel, as well as regular communication with the Norwegian Fishermen's Association. Based on close follow-up and communication, information was to be obtained on the need for a possible hiatus in acquisition on Kvitebjørn, and the proper timing and length of such a pause.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_224
blocks.text: to let mackerel enter the area undisturbed. Little fishing was done in the Oseberg/Kvitebjorn area over the next 12 days. Towards the end of the period the fishery was established closer to land. The Fishermen's Association agreed to the resumption of acquisition on 17 August in confidence that Statoil would pause seismic acquisition at the request of the Fishermen's Association should the situation warrant it. seismic acquisition on Kvitebjørn was later paused from 3 to 5 October due to dense accumulation of purse seiners in the area.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_225
blocks.text: A working group was established consisting of representatives from the Norwegian Fishermen's Association, the Directorate of Fisheries and Statoil, as well as an independent fisheries adviser at Statoil's office. The working group met 1-2 times a week and discussed the fisheries' development.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_226
blocks.text: The Norwegian Fishermen's Association, Statoil and the Directorate of Fisheries later evaluated the project. The season was completed without any major conflicts between troll fishery for mackerel and seismic acquisition. This is a common opinion shared by all parties involved, and the situation has improved compared to previous years. The pilot project has made a decisive contribution to achieving this. In addition, mackerel migration changed in 2012, also contributing to fewer area conflicts. Statoil and the Norwegian Fishermen's Association intend to continue the pilot project in 2013, should seismic acquisition be necessary during the trolling season.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_227
blocks.text: Based on the discussions and recommendations of the working group, Statoil paused seismic acquisition on Kvitebjørn from 5 August

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_228
blocks.text: Fishery expert and escort vessels

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_229
blocks.text: The Petroleum Regulations stipulate that vessels carrying out seismic surveys must have a fishery expert on board when it is necessary for fishing operations in the area8.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_230
blocks.text: The role of the fishery expert

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_231
blocks.text: The fishery expert plays an important role. The person shall actively contribute to enabling the petroleum industry and fisheries to coexist at sea. It is therefore essential for the fisheries expert to be objective in his dealings with all parties, and that he gives his advice on a free and independent basis. The fishery experts shall serve in an advisory capacity to the ship's management, and the management of the survey on the vessel. He shall provide information about any fishery activities in the area, including for example what particularly characterises the drift pattern of the different gear groups, vessel movements and fixed gear.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_232
blocks.text: The fishery expert shall aid communication between the seismic vessel and fishing vessels in the area. He shall be available within the framework of what is reasonable to expect, based on the staffing the licensee has chosen. Advice from fishery experts that is rejected shall be recorded in the log.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_233
blocks.text: The fishery expert shall preferably be involved prior to the survey, but no later than the kick-off meeting, at which the role of the fishery expert shall be clarified. At this meeting, the fishery expert should give a briefing on any expected fishery activities based on obtained information and information contained in the assessment from the Directorate of Fisheries. He shall obtain an overview of the vessels in the area and should well ahead of the start of acquisition contact fishing vessels that may be affected by the seismic surveys and hear their views and what their plans are. Based on this, the seismic acquisition can be adjusted and adapted to the benefit of both industries.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_234
blocks.text: In some cases, the licensee collecting seismic data elects to have two fishery experts on board. The advantage of this is that a fishery expert will then be present on the bridge at all times. It is recommended that the need to have two fishery experts on board is always considered. This can be useful in connection with acquisitions in areas with high fishing activity.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_235
blocks.text: Qualifications of the fishery expert

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_236
blocks.text: To enable the fishery expert to carry out his assignment in a sound manner, it is important that the person has indepth knowledge of the fishery activities. The expert must accordingly meet certain requirements. More information about these requirements is available on NPD's website.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_237
blocks.text: NPD organises courses for fishery experts in collaboration with the Directorate of Fisheries. More information about the course is available on the NPD website. The NPD website also contains a list of qualified fishery experts, along with a manual for fishery experts.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_238
blocks.text: The fishery expert shall keep a log according to a specified format. The logbook must be submitted to the NPD and the Directorate of Fisheries no later than two weeks after the acquisition is concluded.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_239
blocks.text: Section 5 of the Resource Management Regulations

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_240
blocks.text: seismic vessels

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_241
blocks.text: Relevant regulations related to the activities carried out by the vessel on the Norwegian Continental Shelf shall be available on board in Norwegian and English.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_242
blocks.text: The ship's captain, navigators and management of the seismic survey shall familiarise themselves with Norwegian regulations affecting the interaction between seismic activity and fishery activity.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_243
blocks.text: The advisory response from the authorities shall be available on board in Norwegian and English before the survey starts. The ship's captain, navigators and management of the seismic survey shall familiarise themselves with the contents.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_244
blocks.text: Escort vessels

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_245
blocks.text: Escort vessels shall have a passive role vis-à-vis third parties9. This means that escort vessels may not order fishing vessels to move out of the way of the seismic vessel, and that communication with the fishing vessels shall mainly take place via the seismic vessel.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_246
blocks.text: The licensee shall ensure that the crew of the escort vessel has familiarised itself with applicable regulations and Norwegian conditions.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_247
blocks.text: Section 5, subsection eight of the Resource Management Regulations. Coordination meeting and information about the survey to be submitted to the authorities

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_248
blocks.text: Coordination meeting

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_249
blocks.text: Together with industry representatives, the Ministry of Petroleum and Energy and the Ministry of Fisheries and Coastal Affairs will initiate an annual meeting before the survey season starts. The purpose of such meetings is that the authorities must inform companies about matters of importance in terms of time and areas where fish stocks and/or fisheries can be especially affected by seismic surveys. The annual meeting will be held early enough to have a direct bearing on the planning of future seismic surveys.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_250
blocks.text: Notifications that must be sent prior to start-up

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_251
blocks.text: No later than five weeks prior to the start up of survey activities, the licensee shall submit details of the survey to the Norwegian Petroleum Directorate, Directorate of Fisheries, Institute of Marine Research and Ministry of Defence10. The licensee shall report the time and area of the survey. When the State itself collects seismic data these acquisitions shall also be reported according to this system.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_252
blocks.text: On the basis of the information submitted, the authorities will provide advisory feedback within their area of expertise. Thus, to incorporate the consideration of living resources and fishery activities in the best possible manner, the Directorate of Fisheries will comment on any fisheries activity, and the Institute of Marine Research on fish resources, such as spawning. To achieve the most optimal handling of questions about living resources and fishery activity, licensees are advised to contact the Directorate of Fisheries and Institute of Marine Research as early as possible in the planning phase of their seismic surveys.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_253
blocks.text: The NPD provides overall feedback to the licensee. Given the advisory statements that have been made, the licensee should to the extent possible adapt its acquisition in accordance with the advice.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_254
blocks.text: Before the start of each survey the NPD announces the survey area, time period, call sign of the vessel, etc. by publishing this on the NPD website, which also provides an overview of ongoing seismic acquisitions.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_255
blocks.text: It is very important that the licensee carefully considers the time required for the individual survey before submitting the notification. Experience has shown that the extension of surveys is one of the main causes of conflicts. Furthermore, it is important that information about ongoing seismic acquisitions is correct and up to date. The Petroleum Regulations therefore require that changes in surveys must be reported to the authorities. Change means both those situations where the survey starts later than planned, and the situations in which the survey continues beyond the period stipulated. Changes must be reported as soon as possible and no later than ten business days before the scheduled date of termination if the survey is to continue beyond the stipulated period.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_256
blocks.text: Reports to be submitted when the survey is under way

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_257
blocks.text: The licensee shall send reports to the authorities also when the survey is under way. The licensee shall on a weekly basis send information that includes startup, expected conclusion and status of the survey. This information enables the authorities to monitor the activity on the Continental Shelf, and provide updated information.

blocks.text: Tracking of seismic vessels

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_260
blocks.text: Background

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_261
blocks.text: Vessels carrying out seismic surveys shall carry and use equipment that monitors and reports the activity of the vessel, such as satellite tracking equipment and a voyage data recorder11.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_262
blocks.text: Fisheries legislation stipulates that Norwegian fishing vessels with an overall length of 15 metres or more must be able to be tracked. In the Skagerrak, the requirement applies to fishing vessels with an overall length of 12 metres or more operating outside 4 nautical miles from the baseline12. Such tracking of seismic vessels and fishing vessels makes it possible to retrospectively reconstruct movements on the sea, as one of several means of documenting and clarifying allegations about incidents. The Coast Guard will also be able to follow movements in real time. The authorities find that the ability to reconstruct events and conflict situations helps to reduce the level of conflict in connection with the acquisition of seismic data.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_263
blocks.text: Licensees performing seismic surveys in Norwegian waters must contact their contractors at an early stage in order to verify that the vessel that is to collect seismic data has the mandatory equipment and software. The Directorate of Fisheries is the technical operator for tracking seismic vessels.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_264
blocks.text: Position reporting

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_265
blocks.text: An electronic message must be sent from the seismic vessel no later than at the start-up to the Directorate of Fisheries' tracking centre to activate the reception of signals. The vessel shall then automatically report the position of the vessel to the Directorate of Fisheries twice every hour for the duration of the activity. The Directorate of Fisheries may, at the request of the NPD, obtain confirmation of the individual vessel’s position more than twice every hour.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_266
blocks.text: The position report shall contain: unique identification of the vessel,

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_267
blocks.text: the geographical position of the vessel at the time of reporting with a position fault of less than 500 metres and a confidence interval of 99%,

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_268
blocks.text: the time and date of the vessel position, the speed and course at the time of reporting, identification of the type of report submitted

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf

blocks.text: Use and storage of tracking data

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_270
blocks.text: Tracking information received from vessels is saved in a tracking register. The register and rules on the use of the information will ensure that confidentiality issues are adequately addressed.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_271
blocks.text: The register's primary users are authorised personnel in the NPD, the Directorate of Fisheries and the Coast Guard, as well as the Main Rescue Coordination Centre.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_272
blocks.text: The information in the register is protected under the rules of the Public Administration Act pertaining to confidentiality, the Freedom of Information Act and Personal Data Act. More detailed information about tracking equipment on board seismic vessels is found on NPD website.

blocks.text: Compensation scheme for Norwegian fishermen

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_276
blocks.text: Background

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_277
blocks.text: The intention of the Petroleum Regulations is to help ensure joint use of the sea in all phases of the activities. The regulations include a number of measures for achieving this, including impact assessments in advance of the opening of areas to petroleum activities, time and area restrictions on the acquisition of seismic data, the requirement to have a fishery expert onboard seismic vessels and that facilities on the seabed must be overtrawlable. The authorities nevertheless see that offshore petroleum activities on the Shelf may at times inconvenience fishermen. Chapter 8 of the Petroleum Act therefore has special rules on compensation for Norwegian fishermen for financial losses resulting from petroleum activities, including losses resulting from occupied fishing grounds, pollution/waste and losses due to damage caused by facilities. In the exploration phase, compensation for financial losses resulting from occupied fishing grounds will be relevant.

blocks.text: Further details on conditions for compensation

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_287
blocks.text: Occupation of fishing grounds

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_288
blocks.text: Section 8-2, first subsection of the Petroleum Act reads: In the event of petroleum activities within an area entirely or partly occupying a fishing field, the State is obliged, to the extent that fishing becomes impossible or is substantially impeded, to award compensation in respect of any resulting financial loss.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_289
blocks.text: Exploration activities, including seismic acquisitions, are part of the petroleum activities and are therefore covered by the said provision.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_290
blocks.text: Full or partial occupation

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_291
blocks.text: It is a condition for compensation under the provision that petroleum activities wholly or partly occupy a fishing ground. Legislators primarily had occupation as a result of the placement of permanent facilities in mind when the rule was issued. Nevertheless, it cannot be excluded that seismic activity also may be regarded as complete or partial occupation in specific cases, and this is also applied in practice when dealing with compensation claims.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_292
blocks.text: seismic acquisition is, however, a time-limited activity. In this respect, the criterion of whole or partial occupation would only be considered to be met in very special cases.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_293
blocks.text: For the criterion of occupation to be met, the individual fisherman must have a clear connection with the fishing grounds in question, i.e. have fished in the relevant area for some time. The criterion concerning association with the fishing grounds means that the system is most important for fishing operated by small vessels relatively close to land and that they, due to their size and/or equipment have limited opportunities to seek alternative fishing areas. Also larger, ocean-going vessels may in certain circumstances be entitled to compensation, if relevant

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_294
blocks.text: association with the respective fishing grounds is ascertained. The fishing must be made impossible or significantly impeded

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_295
blocks.text: Further, it is a condition that fishing becomes impossible or significantly impeded due to the seismic activity. In other words, any inconvenience will not entitle a fisherman to compensation. For example, fishing is not rendered impossible or substantially impeded if fishing can take place at a reasonable level, without significant additional costs or time lost.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_296
blocks.text: Financial loss

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_297
blocks.text: Each fisherman must prove that he has suffered a financial loss. The financial loss may have occurred as a result of, among others, lost catches and fishing time. Additional expenses that the fisherman has incurred in order to limit his losses or fill his quota, for example by searching for fish in other areas, are covered by the compensation scheme.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_298
blocks.text: It is a general principle of the law of damages to seek to limit one's financial losses. This also applies to compensation under Chapter 8 of the Petroleum Act. Each fisherman is obliged to seek to limit his financial losses. For example, this implies that within reasonable limits, there is an obligation to search for fish in other areas if possible.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_299
blocks.text: The financial loss must be documented. One method of documenting a possible reduced catch can for example be to refer to contract note data for one or more corresponding periods without seismic acquisition, and compare this with contract note data for the period in which seismic acquisition takes place.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_300
blocks.text: Review by commission

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_301
blocks.text: Claims made under Chapter 8 of the Petroleum Act Chapter is dealt with by a commission13. The commission consists of representatives from the fishing industry and the petroleum industry, and is chaired by a representative who meets the requirements to serve as a judge. The composition of the commission shall ensure that both industries are represented, and that the requirements are addressed by representatives who have knowledge of fisheries and petroleum activities.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_302
blocks.text: The commission's decisions may be appealed to an appeals board. The Directorate of Fisheries is the secretariat for the appeals board.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_303
blocks.text: The compensation claims are sent to the appeals board via the Directorate's regional office in the relevant district. The Directorate of Fisheries has prepared a standard form for filing a compensation claim.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_304
blocks.text: Section 8-6 of the Petroleum Act, cf. Chapter 8 of Regulations of 12 December 2008 to Act No. 72 of 29 November 1996 on Petroleum Activities concerning compensation of fishermen.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_305
blocks.text: Guidelines for disagreement

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_306
blocks.text: Licensees who have an exploration or production licence are obliged14 ahead of the impending exploration activity to give notification of the planned survey to the NPD and the Directorate of Fisheries.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_307
blocks.text: In some cases, the directorates may disagree on whether a survey should be carried out as notified or not. This will typically be cases where the Directorate of Fisheries believes the survey cannot be completed out of consideration for the fishery activities. Formally, the licensee has the right to conduct the survey, but it is unfortunate when this takes place contrary to feedback from the authorities. To ensure a comprehensive assessment of these matters, as well as quick resolution, the MFCA and MPE have agreed on guidelines for handling notifications pursuant to Sections 6 and 30, cf. Section 4 of the Resource Management Regulations.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_308
blocks.text: The guidelines facilitate the raising of the issues to the director general level in the directorates, and if agreement cannot be reached here, the NPD shall raise the issue before the MPE for a decision in consultation with the MFCA.

blocks.doc_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf
blocks.block_id: Implementation of seismic surveys on the Norwegian Continental Shelf_309
blocks.text: The MFCA and MPE assume that the directorates will do their utmost to resolve disagreements at the directorate level, and that there will only in exceptional cases be a need to raise the issues to the ministry level.

blocks.text: Reservoir Characterization Using Integration of and Model-Based seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method, "M" Field, East Java Basin

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_1
blocks.text: Haiqa Sabrina Ramadhani1*, Haryono2, Afriadhi Triwerdhana2 1 University of Indonesia, Depok, Indonesia 2 Saka Energi, Jakarta, Indonesia

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_2
blocks.text: *E-mail: haiqa.sabrina@ui.ac.id

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_3
blocks.text: Abstract. seismic inversion is a key technique in reservoir characterization, enabling the transformation of seismic reflection data into quantitative rock property models such as acoustic impedance. This process is essential for enhancing gas field productivity by identifying reservoir features and estimating critical rock parameters. However, conventional inversion methods often struggle to accurately predict complex subsurface properties like porosity and density due to limitations in seismic resolution and the nonlinear nature of rock physics. To overcome these challenges, this study introduces an integrated methodology that combines acoustic impedance-based seismic inversion with Neural Networkdriven multi-attribute analysis to evaluate a gas reservoir in the M Field, East Java Basin. Utilizing high-resolution pre-stack seismic data, the approach estimates the spatial distribution of porosity, density, and velocity. Additionally, the Neural Network analysis is employed to assess a shallower, less-explored interval, characterized by acoustic impedance values between 2948.46 and 3208.68 (g/cc*m/s), porosity levels of 18–20%, sandstone-like density ranging from 1.80 to 1.83 (g/cm³), and Vp/Vs ratios from 1.83 to 1.77. This integrated workflow enhances reservoir prediction accuracy and deepens the understanding of gasbearing zones in the study area.

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_12
blocks.text: The Muriah region, encompassing the Muriah Trough and West-15 Basin along the western margin of the East Java Basin, is recognized as one of the most geologically intricate areas among Indonesia’s back-arc basins. The sedimentary fill of the East Java Basin was shaped by Paleogene extensional tectonics followed by Neogene compressional forces.

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_13
blocks.text: Initial sedimentation in the Muriah area began before the Late Eocene, characterized by the deposition of coarse-grained fluvial and deltaic sediments—such as sands, conglomerates, and coal—within NE-SW oriented half-grabens, forming what is known as the Ngimbang unit. This phase ended due to either tectonic uplift, a global sea level drop, or a combination of both.

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_14
blocks.text: In the Late Eocene, a marine transgression led to widespread flooding and the deposition of limestones and shales of the Ngimbang Formation. However, a subsequent sea level fall and erosion likely removed parts of these deposits, especially in the Muriah area. The onset of the Oligocene brought another transgression, resulting in extensive carbonate sedimentation. In the Muriah region, marginal marine to supratidal environments may have developed during this time. This sequence was interrupted by a compressional event and a significant sea level drop around 30 million years ago, which led to erosion and the removal of much of the earlier deposits.

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_15
blocks.text: Sedimentation resumed in the Late Oligocene with the deposition of the Kujung III Formation, consisting mainly of continental and deltaic sediments. This renewed transgression, driven by extensional tectonics and a global sea level rise beginning around 26 Ma, gradually deepened the depositional environment, culminating in the widespread accumulation of shallow marine carbonates of the Kujung Formation during the Early Miocene.

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_16
blocks.text: A brief regression halted sedimentation in the Early Miocene, but deposition resumed shortly after due to a transgressive trend starting around 21 Ma. This led to the development of carbonate platforms and local buildups, followed by the deposition of marine shales from the Tuban Formation as carbonate production areas were submerged. Uplift during the early Middle Miocene caused localized erosion and structural inversion, particularly in areas with thick Paleogene sequences.

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_17
blocks.text: During the Middle Miocene, sedimentation was influenced by a global sea level decline and increased clastic input due to regional uplift. The Tawun Formation, composed of shales overlain by sands, reflects a shallowing environment transitioning into deltaic shoreface systems—most evident in the Muriah area. A major sea level fall around 10.5 Ma ended this phase, with erosion enhanced by ongoing tectonic activity.

blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_18

blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_25
blocks.text: seismic inversion is a geophysical technique used to transform seismic reflection data into quantitative rock property models, such as acoustic impedance, density, and porosity (Russell, 1988). The methodology begins with seismic data conditioning to preserve amplitude and remove noise, followed by well log integration to calibrate the inversion process through synthetic seismogram generation and wavelet extraction. A low-frequency model, derived from well data and guided by structural interpretation, is then constructed to compensate for the band-limited nature of seismic data. The seismic inversion in this case was performed on high-resolution prestack seismic data, by building an initial model and generating impedance. This process is shown in figure 3.

blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_27
blocks.text: The Neural Network multi-attribute analysis methodology involves using machine learning algorithms to establish nonlinear relationships between multiple seismic attributes and petrophysical properties derived from well logs. In this study, the process begins by selecting relevant seismic attributes—such as amplitude, phase, frequency, and acoustic impedance—from pre-stack seismic data that show good correlation with target reservoir properties like porosity and density. These attributes are then statistically analyzed to determine their predictive strength,

blocks.doc_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method
blocks.block_id: Integration of and Model-Based Seismic Inversion and Neural Network Method_28
blocks.text: followed by normalization to ensure consistency across datasets A supervised learning model, typically a feedforward neural network, is trained using well log data as ground truth. The network learns the underlying nonlinear patterns between the selected attributes and the desired property (e.g., porosity or density) through iterative backpropagation and error minimization. Once the model is trained and validated using blind wells or cross-validation techniques, it is applied across the seismic volume to generate property prediction volumes. This methodology enables high-resolution, data-driven reservoir characterization by leveraging both seismic and well data in a predictive framework, especially in complex or under-explored intervals where traditional inversion techniques may fall short. This process is shown in figure 4.

blocks.text: Abstract

blocks.doc_id: Integration of Deterministic Seismic inversion with Machine Learning
blocks.block_id: Integration of Deterministic Seismic inversion with Machine Learning_3
blocks.text: seismic inversion plays a key role in reservoir characterization. The inversion allows interpreters to transfer data from interface properties to layers and physical properties. Various deterministic approaches are available for interpreters to achieve this objective, including model-based, trace-based, recursive approaches, etc. Machine learning methods are increasingly adopted in reservoir characterization workflows to identify nonlinear and complicated relationships between various parameters, helping to predict one parameter from another or combine one with others.

blocks.doc_id: Integration of Deterministic Seismic inversion with Machine Learning
blocks.block_id: Integration of Deterministic Seismic inversion with Machine Learning_4
blocks.text: In this study, we employ pre-stack model-based inversion to invert seismic data for P-wave and S-wave impedances. We extract numerous seismic attributes from the seismic data and use them to train a Feedforward Neural Network to predict the computed impedances at well locations. We compare the impedance models from deterministic inversion with those produced by the ANN. The resulting models are validated using wells that were not included in the inversion or ANN training. The ANN demonstrates good capability to reproduce results close to the inversion results. Next, the P-wave and S-wave impedance models are used for a detailed characterization of the fluvial-deltaic reservoir in the study area. Various quantities are derived, including Poisson ratio, Bulk modulus, Shear modulus, Lambda-Rho, and Mu-Rho. All models are combined using another ANN that has been trained to classify the area of interest into reservoir and non-reservoir facies. The trained ANN allows us to delineate potential reservoir facies and identify some new zones that are not drilled.

blocks.doc_id: Integration of Deterministic Seismic inversion with Machine Learning
blocks.block_id: Integration of Deterministic Seismic inversion with Machine Learning_5
blocks.text: In conclusion, the ANN emerges as a key player in reservoir characterization. The above study's methodology can be applied to other fields. As the proposed workflow is data-driven, better results can be achieved than those in the present study.
